name: How to Plan and Execute a Bathroom Countertop Replacement Step by Step

step.name: Step 1: Confirm base cabinets are secured and dead level
step.text: Lay a long spirit level across the entire length and width of the vanity cabinets. Insert shims underneath the cabinet floor base if needed, securing the units firmly to the wall studs so there is zero flexing or movement when bearing heavy stone weight.

step.name: Step 2: Create a precise physical or digital template
step.text: Measure the exact cabinet perimeter, noting any out-of-square wall conditions, drywall bows, and required overhangs. Trace your sink bowl cutout lines and faucet hole positions carefully to verify proper under-sink clearances with the cabinet framing.

step.name: Step 3: Perform a dry fit of the fabricated countertop
step.text: Carefully set the countertop on top of the cabinet bases without any adhesive to verify flush seams against the wall. Check that mirror frames clear the top and that sink cutouts align perfectly over the plumbing supply lines and drain rough-in.

step.name: Step 4: Mount the sink and apply structural adhesive
step.text: Set undermount sinks using appropriate mounting clips and sealant if pre-mounting, or secure drop-in fixtures as planned. Run continuous beads of manufacturer-approved silicone or construction adhesive along the top edges of the cabinet carcass before setting the final stone top in position.

step.name: Step 5: Apply joint sealant and allow complete curing
step.text: Position your backsplash pieces, seal all seams with mold-resistant silicone, and smooth the joint beads cleanly. Allow the adhesive to cure undisturbed for the recommended curing window before connecting water lines or running the faucet to verify a leak-free setup.
